page: Amazon Web Services i8ge.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, storage-optimized server powered by 192 dedicated physical cores of the ARMv9 AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 architecture. Operating at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz, this arm64 processor features 2 MB of L2 cache per core and 36 MB of L3 cache. The system is equipped with 1536.0 GB of DDR5 memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. It includes a massive local storage capacity of 120,000 GB delivered via NVMe SSDs, alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 300 Gbps. No GPUs are present on this instance.

In benchmark evaluations, the i8ge.metal-48xl demonstrates top-tier performance across multi-core processing, memory bandwidth, and database operations. The server achieves top-decile results in stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, passmark database operations, and redis SET operations, which registers at 378.59 million operations per second. Memory bandwidth tests for both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks also rank in the top ten percent. However, single-threaded tasks, such as stress-ng single-core CPU performance and geekbench text processing, fall into the average tier, and LLM text generation for a small model is positioned in the bottom ten percent.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers high resource density by bundling massive local NVMe SSD storage and high-capacity DDR5 memory with a 192-core ARM processor. This configuration reduces the need for external storage attachments, optimizing the cost-per-gigabyte ratio for data-heavy deployments. The hardware profile is highly suited for large-scale databases, high-throughput static web serving, software compilation, and multi-threaded data decompression tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services i8ge.metal-48xl is a storage-optimized bare-metal server featuring 192 dedicated ARMv9 AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 physical cores running at 2.7 GHz. It is equipped with 1536.0 GB of DDR5 memory and a massive local storage capacity of 120,000 GB via NVMe SSDs, supported by a 300 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The server delivers top-tier multi-core CPU performance, exceptional memory bandwidth, and outstanding database operations, as evidenced by top-decile results in redis SET operations and passmark database benchmarks. While single-core performance and LLM text generation are average to poor, the high density of local storage and memory makes this instance highly cost-efficient for data-intensive deployments. It is best suited for large-scale databases, high-throughput web serving, and intensive multi-threaded workloads.
